precepts.text: Jacob said give me my wife that I may go in unto her, Laban made a feast and brought Leah to him, and he went in unto her; the feast is the coming together.
precepts.point: Why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he had not impregnated, and if she had committed adultery why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question; he hid her because the child was his.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Matthew says Mary was espoused to Joseph, and “before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost.” What does “came together” mean? Genesis 29 shows the custom. Jacob served seven years for Rachel, then said, “Give me my wife, for my days are fulfilled, that I may go in unto her.” “And Laban gathered together all the men of the place, and made a feast. And it came to pass in the evening, that he took Leah his daughter, and brought her to him; and he went in unto her.”

The feast is the coming together. Coming together was the customary wedding feast, the same custom seen with Tobit. So before Joseph and Mary came together in the wedding feast, they lay together. There was no fornication, because they were already espoused. Espousal is marriage: once the father made the promise, she could not go and marry another, and a man who lies with a betrothed woman commits adultery. That is why the angel called Mary Joseph's wife. She was his wife by espousal, not because he had lain with her; sex alone does not make a marriage.

Then “Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily.” The commentators say that means he meant to divorce her secretly, because the child was not his. But if a just man's espoused wife were pregnant by another man, the law said she must die; a just man would not hide her. Put her away privily means hide her, the way “Elisabeth conceived, and hid herself five months.” A public example means being put to death in public. Had Mary gone back to her father's house showing, they would have said she played the harlot, just as they said of Tamar at three months.

So here is the question: why would a just man hide a pregnant woman he did not impregnate? And if she had committed adultery, why would a just man hide her sin? There is no way around that question. Minded means he was thinking about it: he was going to hide her so nothing would happen to her for what the two of them had done, because the child was his.

precepts.text: I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels; the promised king comes out of David's bowels.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
The Lord promised David a king out of his own body: “And when thy days be fulfilled, and thou shalt sleep with thy fathers, I will set up thy seed after thee, which shall proceed out of thy bowels, and I will establish his kingdom.”

The seed that proceeds out of David's bowels is the promised king. So when the angel came to Joseph in the dream, he called him “Joseph, thou son of David”. The line is Joseph's, David's line.

The angel said, “fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy of 2 Samuel: the seed promised to David, coming out of his bowels.

That is why the Nativity begins with the bloodline. The child Mary conceived is the fulfilling of the promise made to David, that God would set up his seed after him and establish his kingdom.

precepts.text: The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David, of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
The promise to David was sworn: “The Lord hath sworn in truth unto David; he will not turn from it; Of the fruit of thy body will I set upon thy throne.”

The Lord swore it in truth, and he will not turn from it. The king on David's throne would be the fruit of David's body. That is the same promise as 2 Samuel 7:12, the seed that shall proceed out of David's bowels.

So when the angel said to Joseph, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost”, that which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the fruit of David's body that the Lord swore to set upon his throne. The line runs through Joseph, the son of David.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” The son is the fruit of David's body, sworn in truth, set on David's throne.

precepts.text: God had sworn to David that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne; according to the flesh, not the spirit.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Peter said of David: “Therefore being a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn with an oath to him, that of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh, he would raise up Christ to sit on his throne”.

God swore to David that of the fruit of his loins he would raise up Christ, and notice the words: according to the flesh. Not according to the spirit. Christ sits on David's throne as the fruit of David's loins in the flesh.

That is why the angel spoke to “Joseph, thou son of David”, and why “that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost” means it is of the prophecy: the promise sworn to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132 that the king would come out of his bowels, the fruit of his body.

So the child of Matthew 1 is the Christ God swore to raise up of the fruit of David's loins, according to the flesh, to sit on his throne. The bloodline is the birthright.

precepts.text: Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh; made flesh and blood like his brethren.
precepts.point: In Isaiah 7 Ahaz would not ask a sign, so the Lord gave one: a virgin shall conceive and bear a son named Immanuel, and before the child knew to refuse the evil the land of the two kings, Syria and Ephraim, would be forsaken; the sign was the child.

note.label: The Nativity: the Bloodline, Birthright, & the Messiah

precepts.why:
Paul says it plainly: “Concerning his Son Jesus Christ our Lord, which was made of the seed of David according to the flesh”. According to what? The flesh.

According to the flesh, he was made like you and I: made flesh and blood like unto his brethren, like his children. The same thing.

That is how Matthew 1 reads. Joseph was minded to put Mary away privily, “But while he thought on these things”, not did them but only thought about doing them, the angel appeared to him saying, “Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost.” That which is conceived in her is of the prophecy: the seed promised to David in 2 Samuel 7 and Psalm 132, of the fruit of his loins according to the flesh.

So Jesus Christ our Lord was made of the seed of David according to the flesh. He came into this world as a son of man, made flesh and blood like his brethren, and that is how he fulfils the promise to David.

note.label: We Are Born in Babylon

precepts.why:
Matthew traces the line “after they were brought to Babylon”: Jechonias begat Salathiel, Salathiel begat Zorobabel, and on down to “Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ.” That is the Branch, right through Zerubbabel.

In the sit down with Captain Matathias and Captain Galiah, the dude with that stupid hat said there was a curse on Jeconiah that nobody of his seed would sit as king, so the genealogy is ruled out. Think. After Jeconiah, was there a king in Israel sitting on the throne? No. When Babylon came in, that was it. Zedekiah came, and they got rid of him and killed him with his sons. There was no king during the time of Christ.

John shows it: “When Jesus therefore perceived that they would come and take him by force, to make him a king, he departed again into a mountain himself alone.” That is how much Israel loved him. They said, we want him to be our king. He said no.

Why? Because the prophets said there would be no more king until Christ returns. The sceptre was held for Shiloh, the Messiah, “and unto him shall the gathering of the people be.” Christ would not be made king by force before the time, so the line through Jeconiah and Zerubbabel is not ruled out; it runs straight to the one king still to sit on the throne.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
We did not return to what the Most High commanded, the feasts he told us to go back to, and that is why we were in need of a saviour, an ultimate sacrifice. From Abraham to David, from David to the carrying away into Babylon, and from Babylon to Christ were fourteen generations each; we were always in slavery.

“And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His name means he saves. His people: the Israelites only. From their sins. That is why he was the ultimate sacrifice.

His cousin John expounds on it: “Behold the Lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world.” The Lamb of God. Christ was that perfect, ultimate sacrifice, the lamb that takes away the sins of the people he came to save.

precepts.text: Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me. The animal sacrifices were temporary, a shadow training us for what was to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ. Lo, I come in the volume of the book: the whole book, because Christ is present in the Old Testament and before it.
precepts.point: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. His people; that is who the sacrifice was for.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
To expound further on Christ being the ultimate sacrifice: “Wherefore when he cometh into the world, he saith, Sacrifice and offering thou wouldest not, but a body hast thou prepared me”. The body was Christ. The sacrificial laws of animal sacrifice were a preparation for what was to come, a shadow of good things to come; the good thing that came was the body of Jesus Christ, dying only for the nation of Israel.

“In burnt offerings and sacrifices for sin thou hast had no pleasure.” The Most High had no pleasure in those sacrifices. They were temporary, to train us and prepare us for Christ.

“Then said I, Lo, I come (in the volume of the book it is written of me,) to do thy will, O God.” In the volume of the book: the whole book, not just the New Testament. Christ is present in the Old Testament, and Christ is present before the Old Testament.

“Above when he said, Sacrifice and offering and burnt offerings and offering for sin thou wouldest not, neither hadst pleasure therein; which are offered by the law”. So the offerings of the law pointed to the body prepared for him, the one sacrifice that saves his people from their sins.

precepts.point: Thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins. His people; that is who the sacrifice was for.

note.label: 70 Times 7: The Perfection of Mercy Through Christ

precepts.why:
Christ was always the plan. He is the author, the executive producer, whatever title you want to give him. From before the Old Testament, the body prepared for him in the volume of the book was the plan for saving his people from their sins.

John shows it: “All things were made by him”. All things were made by Christ: the principalities, the things you see out in space, the worlds, with an s. “And without him was not any thing made that was made.”

The one who made all things is the one who came as the Lamb of God to save his people. The sacrifices of the law, the seventh day and the rest it points to were all his from the beginning. So when the angel said “thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins”, it was the Maker of all things coming to fulfil the plan that was always his.

note.label: Fixx Ya Face Fridays | as Was Supposed!!

precepts.why:
Matthew 1 is “The book of the generation of Jesus Christ, the son of David, the son of Abraham”: the link between Christ and the royal seat promised through David's loins, through Solomon and their sons. At the end of it: “Eliud begat Eleazar; and Eleazar begat Matthan; and Matthan begat Jacob; And Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary”. Someone claimed Jacob and Heli were brothers. You do not read that anywhere in the Bible.

Luke 3: “And Jesus himself began to be about thirty years of age, being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph, which was the son of Heli”. Did it say the son of Heli? No. “As was supposed” refers to him being the son of Joseph. It had nothing to do with Heli at all.

Now line them up. Luke goes on: “Which was the son of Matthat, which was the son of Levi, which was the son of Melchi”. Even if Matthat and Matthan were the same man spelled differently, Matthan's father in Matthew is Eleazar, and in Luke Matthat's father is Levi. Eliud and Eleazar are not mentioned in Luke 3 at all. These are two completely different bloodlines. They do not expect you to bounce back and forth and make sure it lines up; they bank on you not fact-checking.

Matthew starts with Joseph: the angel comes to Joseph, you follow his story, and his lineage is given. Luke chose to follow Mary: it begins with her cousin Elisabeth and the babe leaping in her womb, and in the third chapter it gives her lineage, all men. That is why not one woman is named in Luke 3, while some women are named in Matthew 1. Where it would have said Mary, it names her husband.

And “Booz begat Obed of Ruth” is where the levirate marriage actually shows up, but we will not be bamboozled by a spin move into an Old Testament law that has nothing to do with the question. Not knowing something does not make you an idiot. Pick up the phone and ask a Bishop or a Deacon. Making it up does.

precepts.point: Keep the flower of thine age sound, give not thy strength to strangers, and sow thine own seed, that thy race may be magnified.

note.label: 2025 Recap: Different Times, Same Truth

precepts.why:
A well-respected black theologian, preaching before white people all over the place, taught that race is a social construct and not a biblical concept. False. The Bible is the family tree; Genesis 10 is the table of nations. Sirach says: “My son, keep the flower of thine age sound; and give not thy strength to strangers”: keep your seed, your nobility, your race, and don’t pollute it with other nations. “When thou hast gotten a fruitful possession through all the field”, find your wife, “sow it with thine own seed, trusting in the goodness of thy stock.” Seed and race are the same thing. “So thy race which thou leavest shall be magnified, having the confidence of their good descent.” So what is he talking about? These pastors don’t know the Bible, and he never opened it once.

Matthew shows who Christ came for: “And she shall bring forth a son, and thou shalt call his name JESUS: for he shall save his people from their sins.” His people. You go to somebody’s house and they say, that’s his people: that means his family, his kinfolk. The Bible was written by black people, and kindred and kinfolk are all in it.

Christ came to save his own race. He never came for any other race or nation. That is why the old family Bibles had the whole lineage written in them.

Yes, we all come from Adam, but Ezra makes the difference: of Adam come we all, “And the people also whom thou hast chosen.” As for the other people which also come of Adam, “thou hast said that they are nothing.” God chose a people out of Adam, and those are the people Christ came to save from their sins. Time is up on the Christian church.
